messages:
jen: Quick heads-up — rolled the new windowed-prefix-store to canary (20% of serving prod) :tada:
jen: Early numbers look pretty solid: p99 down ~34%, p50 down ~10%, token cost down ~18% across multi-turn convo workloads. Details below.

infra-bot: Canary metrics snapshot (last 30m):
```
model: redwood-v2-large
traffic: 20% canary
p50_latency_before: 42ms
p50_latency_after: 38ms
p95_latency_before: 210ms
p95_latency_after: 160ms
p99_latency_before: 820ms
p99_latency_after: 540ms
token_cost_before: $0.0084
token_cost_after: $0.0069
kv_prefix_hitrate_before: 27%
kv_prefix_hitrate_after: 46%
errors: 0.02% -> 0.025% (investigating)
```

ryan: sick win. can you paste the exact rollout command and the config we used?
jen: sure — canary command we used: `rcli rollout start --policy windowed-prefix-store --canary 20 --regions all --model redwood-v2-large`
jen: relevant config snippet: 
```
windowed_prefix_store:
  enabled: true
  window_size: 64
  eviction_policy: least_recent_prefix
  min_prefix_tokens: 4
  adapt_thresh: 0.75
```

maya: nice. any memory/regression tradeoffs? hit rate improvements look legit.
jen: hit rate jumped for prefixes >=8 tokens. memory rose ~2% on canary nodes (mostly metadata), but overall CPU/GPU utilization dropped a bit because fewer recomputes.

alex: saw the note about errors bump — what were they? transient gRPC timeouts?
jen: digging in. looks like 3 small spikes tied to a single host in eu-west-1 during a rolling update. we isolated and rolled back that host from the canary. no customer impact.

eng-sre: logged an incident (INC-2027) to track the eu-west host; added short-term alert to catch >5% request failures from any single host in canary pools.

ken: can we enable this for Dedicated clusters? any special flags for on-prem?
jen: should be compatible; the key is the runtime's prefix-store feature flag. for Dedicated/Private we exposed `runtime.features.windowed_prefix_store=true` in the node bootstrap config. recommend testing with a 5% canary first.

ryan: timeline? when do we push to 100%?
jen: plan is to promote to 50% tomorrow morning if canary stays stable, 100% on Tue next week. running the long-tail eval suite tonight against held-out prompt set to validate quality regressions.

maya: can you drop a 1-pager on perf KPIs for the exec sync? would be great to have cost delta + customer impact in one slide.
jen: will do — short doc + a chart. ping me if you want early access.

alex: outstanding work. big win for latency-sensitive customers. :clap: :rocket:
jen: thanks team! monitoring continues. will post an update after the long-tail run.
